paras: The police shooting of Dan Howard took place in Birmingham, Alabama, about 11:30 p.m. on 16 August 1905, when Policeman Ray shot Howard, a Black man, as he ran from arrest. Howard was wounded in the abdomen and first reported likely to die, but a day later physicians said he had a chance to recover.

According to the Birmingham Age-Herald, Policemen Ray and Elledge were patrolling their beat about 11 p.m. when a young Black boy told them that Howard had shot at his sister, Rana Stovall. A second report said instead that Howard, "it is said," had shot at "his sister" on Eleventh street and Fourth avenue.

The two officers went to Howard's house at Eleventh street and Fourth avenue, but before they could handcuff him he broke loose and ran up the street. By the officers' account, both ordered him to stop, and when he did not, Ray drew his pistol and fired three shots. One .38-caliber ball entered the right side of Howard's lower abdomen and came out at the back of his hip.

Howard was taken to the police station and then to a hospital, named as St. Vincent's in the first report and as the Hillman hospital in the second. Police docketed a charge of assault with intent to murder against him. On 18 August the paper reported that he had rested well, had little fever and might "pull through." The coverage does not show his later condition or any inquiry into the shooting.

The shooting appears only in the Birmingham Age-Herald, which ran it as a local police item on 17 and 18 August under the headlines "Negro Man Is Shot by Policeman Ray" and "Negro May Recover." Both items printed the officers' version as fact, stating that Howard was shot "while attempting to escape," and neither gave any account from Howard or other witnesses. No coverage of the shooting was found in the Black press.

accounts.label: Police account
accounts.gist: A boy told patrolling officers that Howard had shot at his sister; when the officers went to Howard's house he broke loose before being handcuffed, ignored orders to stop, and Ray shot him.

framing.detail: The Age-Herald ran the shooting as a local police item ('NEGRO MAN IS SHOT BY POLICEMAN RAY', 'NEGRO MAY RECOVER'), stating as fact that Howard was shot 'while attempting to escape'.

conflicts.note: The two reports in the same paper name different hospitals; he may have been moved, but neither says so.
